English

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

madeira (countable and uncountable, plural madeiras)

  1. Alternative letter-case form of Madeira (“fortified wine”).

Anagrams

[edit]
  • Demaria, Maredia

Fala

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • maeira (Mañegu)
  • meira (Lagarteiru)

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Galician-Portuguese madeira, from Latin māteria.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /maˈdei̯ɾa/
  • Rhymes: -ei̯ɾa
  • Syllabification: ma‧dei‧ra

Noun

[edit]

madeira f (plural madeiras)

  1. (Valverdeñu) wood

References

[edit]
  • Valeš, Miroslav (2021), Diccionariu de A Fala: lagarteiru, mañegu, valverdeñu (web)‎[1], 2nd edition, Minde, Portugal: CIDLeS, published 2022, →ISBN, page 192

Galician

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Galician-Portuguese madeira, from Latin materia. Cf. also materia.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /maˈdejɾa/ [mɐˈð̞ej.ɾɐ]
  • Rhymes: -ejɾa
  • Hyphenation: ma‧dei‧ra

Noun

[edit]

madeira f (plural madeiras)

  1. (uncountable) wood (material)
    Hoxe aquel recuncho cerca Unha reixa de madeira.
    Today that corner is surrounded by a fence of wood.

References

[edit]
  • “madeira”, in Dicionario da Real Academia Galega (in Galician), A Coruña: Royal Galician Academy, 2012–2026
  • Seoane, Ernesto Xosé González; Granja, María Álvarez de la; Agrelo, Ana Isabel Boullón (2006–2022), “madeira”, in Dicionario de Dicionarios do galego medieval [Dictionary of dictionaries of Medieval Galician] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Barreiro, Xavier Varela; Guinovart, Xavier Gómez (2006–2018), “madeira”, in Corpus Xelmírez: corpus lingüístico da Galicia medieval [Corpus Xelmírez: linguistic corpus of Medieval Galicia] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, editor (2006–2013), “madeira”, in Dicionario de Dicionarios da lingua galega [Dictionary of Dictionaries of the Galician language] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Rosario Álvarez Blanco, editor (2014–2024), “madeira”, in Tesouro do léxico patrimonial galego e portugués (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega, →ISSN

Portuguese

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /maˈde(j).ɾɐ/ [maˈde(ɪ̯).ɾɐ]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /maˈde(j).ɾɐ/ [maˈde(ɪ̯).ɾɐ]
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /maˈde(j).ɾa/ [maˈde(ɪ̯).ɾa]
 
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /mɐˈdɐj.ɾɐ/ [mɐˈðɐj.ɾɐ]
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /mɐˈdɐj.ɾɐ/ [mɐˈðɐj.ɾɐ]
    • (Northern Portugal) IPA(key): /mɐˈdej.ɾɐ/ [mɐˈðej.ɾɐ]
    • (Central Portugal) IPA(key): /mɐˈdej.ɾɐ/ [mɐˈðej.ɾɐ]
    • (Southern Portugal) IPA(key): /mɐˈde.ɾɐ/ [mɐˈðe.ɾɐ]

  • Rhymes: -ejɾɐ, (Portugal) -ɐjɾɐ
  • Homophone: Madeira
  • Hyphenation: ma‧dei‧ra

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese madeira, from Latin māteria, from Proto-Indo-European *méh₂tēr (“mother”). Doublet of matéria, a learned borrowing. Cognates include Galician madeira and Spanish madera.

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • madeyra (obsolete)

Noun

[edit]

madeira f (plural madeiras)

  1. (uncountable) wood (substance making up the central part of the trunk and branches of a tree)
    Synonyms: lenha, lenho, pau
  2. wood (the wood of a particular species of tree)
    Synonym: pau
  3. a piece of timber
    Synonym: pau
  4. (music, usually in the plural) woodwind instrument
Derived terms
[edit]

Interjection

[edit]

madeira!

  1. timber!; used by lumberjacks to warn others when a tree is falling down

Etymology 2

[edit]

Shortening of vinho da Madeira (literally “wine of Madeira”), after the Portuguese island of Madeira.

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • Madeira

Noun

[edit]

madeira m (uncountable)

  1. a type of fortified wine produced in the island of Madeira
    Synonyms: vinho da Madeira, vinho Madeira

Etymology 3

[edit]

See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

Verb

[edit]

madeira

  1. inflection of madeirar:
    1. third-person singular present indicative
    2. second-person singular imperative
